verses.1: For the leader. A psalm of David. I LORD, you have probed me, you know me:
verses.2: you know when I sit and stand; you understand my thoughts from afar.
verses.3: My travels and my rest you mark; with all my ways you are familiar.
verses.4: Even before a word is on my tongue, LORD, you know it all.
verses.5: Behind and before you encircle me and rest your hand upon me.
verses.6: Such knowledge is beyond me, far too lofty for me to reach.
verses.7: Where can I hide from your spirit? From your presence, where can I flee?
verses.8: If I ascend to the heavens, you are there; if I lie down in Sheol, you are there too.
verses.9: If I fly with the wings of dawn and alight beyond the sea,
verses.10: Even there your hand will guide me, your right hand hold me fast.
verses.11: If I say, "Surely darkness shall hide me, and night shall be my light"
verses.12: Darkness is not dark for you, and night shines as the day. Darkness and light are but one.
verses.13: You formed my inmost being; you knit me in my mother's womb.
verses.14: I praise you, so wonderfully you made me; wonderful are your works! My very self you knew;
verses.15: my bones were not hidden from you, When I was being made in secret, fashioned as in the depths of the earth.
verses.16: Your eyes foresaw my actions; in your book all are written down; my days were shaped, before one came to be.
verses.17: How precious to me are your designs, O God; how vast the sum of them!
verses.18: Were I to count, they would outnumber the sands; to finish, I would need eternity.
verses.19: If only you would destroy the wicked, O God, and the bloodthirsty would depart from me!
verses.20: Deceitfully they invoke your name; your foes swear faithless oaths.
verses.21: Do I not hate, LORD, those who hate you? Those who rise against you, do I not loathe?
verses.22: With fierce hatred I hate them, enemies I count as my own.
verses.23: Probe me, God, know my heart; try me, know my concerns.
verses.24: See if my way is crooked, then lead me in the ancient paths.

notes.text: When I sit and stand: in all my physical movement.
Fly with the wings of dawn: go to the extremities of the east. Beyond the sea: uttermost bounds of the west; the sea is the Mediterranean.
Night shall be my light: night to me is what day is to others.
The depths of the earth: figurative language for the womb, stressing the hidden and mysterious operations that occur there.
My way... the ancient paths: the manner of living of our ancestors, who were faithful to God's will. Cf Jeremiah 6:16.
